dossier.candidate: AI-enabled productized services for local small businesses (websites, Google Business Profile optimization, review-response management, AI chatbot/receptionist, missed-call text-back, social content packages)
dossier.summary: The owner would sell fixed-scope digital services to local SMBs in the GTA (restaurants, trades, clinics, salons, Korean-owned businesses), with the AI doing most of the build work. Canadian prices seen in 2025-2026 search results: small-business websites cost CAD $500-$3,000 from freelancers and $3,000-$15,000+ from agencies. Google Business Profile management runs about CAD $285-$475/month at one Canadian agency. Social media packages average about $500-$850/month. The upside is that capital needs are low (software only, no vehicle or inventory) and the AI can do much of the delivery. The problems: (1) The average cold-email reply rate is only about 3.43% (Instantly 2026 benchmark). No sourced close-rate or sales-cycle data for local SMBs was found. (2) CASL puts the burden of proving consent on the sender, and the conspicuous-publication exemption is narrow and judged case by case. Penalties go up to $1M per violation for individuals and $10M for businesses. (3) The 'AI automation agency' niche is crowded with courses and hype. Community summaries (anecdotal) say most people who start never reach meaningful revenue. (4) SMBs can buy the underlying tools directly and cheaply (AI receptionists from $49/month, DIY site builders at $25-$60/month). Reselling a platform like GoHighLevel can leave thin or negative margin at a $199/month price. Reaching CAD $5k/month net within 60 days needs about 8+ closed deals, or about 17 retainers at around $300/month. That is possible for a strong salesperson but unlikely for most people starting from zero. RESEARCH LIMITS: WebFetch was blocked by the egress proxy on every domain tried (crtc.gc.ca, laws-lois.justice.gc.ca, ised-isde.canada.ca, canada.ca, instantly.ai, tomba.io, mcinnescooper.com, ciela.ai, gohighlevel.com, wikipedia.org, reddit.com). The session-wide search budget (200) also ran out after this agent's 10th search. So every fact below comes from search-result titles and snippets I saw, not from full pages I opened. Where a snippet could have come from more than one page in a result set, the attribution is flagged as uncertain.
dossier.time_to_first_revenue: No sourced sales-cycle benchmark for local SMB services was found. ESTIMATE, using the sourced 3.43% average reply rate (https://instantly.ai/cold-email-benchmark-report-2026) and two UNSOURCED assumptions (30% of replies are positive; 20% of positive replies close): emails per closed deal = 1 / (0.0343 x 0.30 x 0.20) = 1 / 0.002058 ≈ 486. At 50 compliant emails per working day, that is about 486 / 50 ≈ 10 working days of sending per deal. After that comes the time to collect a deposit and build. ESTIMATE: first cash in about 2-5 weeks, assuming the owner also does in-person or phone follow-up and takes a deposit up front. This is a judgment built on unsourced conversion assumptions, not measured data.

dossier.path_to_5k_math: All of the following is ESTIMATE; prices are sourced, conversion rates are assumed. (A) Retainers only. Price a 'Local Presence Care' retainer (GBP posts, review responses, small site edits) at CAD $300/month, near Storyteller Media's CAN$285 Essentials package. With near-zero direct cost: $5,000 / $300 = 16.7, so about 17 retainers. If each client needs a GoHighLevel sub-account, the cost per sub-account is $1,500-$3,000 / 10 = $150-$300 (currency likely USD). The margin on $300 then falls to $0-$150, so you would need $5,000 / $150 ≈ 34 clients or more. So avoid building the base offer on per-client GHL. (B) Website builds only. At CAD $1,500 (within the $500-$3,000 freelancer range): $5,000 / $1,500 = 3.3, so 4 new builds every month, with no compounding. (C) Blended by about day 60: 3 builds x $1,500 = $4,500, plus 5 retainers x $300 = $1,500, gives $6,000 gross. Minus about $300-$700 in software (unsourced) leaves about $5,300-$5,700 net. That needs about 8 closed deals in about 8 weeks. Funnel: 3.43% reply rate (sourced) x 30% positive (assumed) x 20% close (assumed) = 0.206% of emails become deals, so about 486 emails per deal. 8 deals x 486 ≈ 3,900 CASL-compliant emails over about 40 working days ≈ 97 per day. Each address must be individually vetted for conspicuous publication, and deliverability limits apply. Month 2 onward is only sustainable if retainers accumulate faster than churn, and churn data was not found. Conclusion (ESTIMATE): hitting $5k net by day 60 needs sales performance well above the average benchmark, or warm or in-person channels such as Korean-community networks, whose conversion data was not found.

regulations.fact: CASL implied consent by conspicuous publication applies only if (a) the person conspicuously published the electronic address, (b) the publication did not come with a statement that they do not want unsolicited commercial electronic messages, and (c) the message is relevant to the person's business, role, functions or duties in a business or official capacity

The CRTC says the conspicuous-publication exemption sets a higher standard than simple public availability of an address. It is not a broad licence to contact any address found online, and it is judged case by case
Under CASL the sender must prove consent. A sender relying on conspicuous publication must show how its situation meets the implied-consent criteria

A commercial electronic message needs three things: consent, identification information, and an unsubscribe mechanism. The message must identify the sender (and anyone it is sent on behalf of) and give contact information valid for at least 60 days
The unsubscribe link must stay valid for at least 60 days after sending. Requests must be processed without delay and no later than 10 business days after receipt
CASL penalties go up to $1M per violation for an individual and up to $10M per violation for a corporation
The CRTC has issued a $1.1 million CASL penalty (law firm article title; case details not opened)

A 2026 compliance blog says cold email is not automatically illegal in Canada but only works under narrow implied-consent rules (existing business relationships, conspicuously published business addresses tied to a relevant role). This is a secondary source

The following were NOT verified in this session (official pages egress-blocked): whether CASL covers SMS outreach, the status of CASL's private right of action, whether cold phone calls fall under CASL or under the National DNCL instead, privacy and consent rules for AI receptionists that record calls, and the GST/HST small-supplier threshold

dossier.score_rationale: Speed 5: no licence or capital barrier, and the AI can build a demo site in hours. But first cash depends on the owner closing a sale, and no sales-cycle data was found; the ESTIMATE of 2-5 weeks rests on unsourced conversion assumptions. Probability of $5k/month within 60 days, 2.5: the math needs about 8 closed deals in 8 weeks, or about 17 retainers. At the sourced 3.43% average reply rate, that means about 3,900 individually CASL-vetted emails. Community evidence (anecdotal) says most people who start never reach meaningful revenue, and direct-to-SMB SaaS undercuts pricing. The score would rise if the owner has existing SMB relationships or strong Korean-community networks, but no data quantifies that. Capital-light 8.5: software only, with sourced GHL plans at $97-$297/mo, and even those are optional. AI leverage 7: the AI can produce most of the delivery (sites, GBP content, review replies, scripts, templates), but selling, account verification, payments, and client relationships are human-only, and sales is the bottleneck. Low risk 5.5: little financial downside, but CASL penalties are large in theory (up to $1M per violation for individuals) with the onus on the sender, and there is liability exposure from AI receptionists or chatbots speaking for clients. Evidence quality caveat: the egress proxy blocked full-page reads, so all facts come from search-result snippets.

hidden_costs_or_blockers: The sales bottleneck is unmitigated. The owner's English level, sales experience and network are unknown, and the AI cannot call, visit or close. If the owner is not comfortable selling in English (or has no Korean-business network), the probability of reaching $5k is near zero.

The goal was not met, by the dossier's own math: its 60-day scenario averages about $3k/month (ESTIMATE: $6,000 / 2 months). Reaching $5k/month sustained needs about 3+ closes every month plus retainers accumulating faster than churn, and there is no churn benchmark.

Ramp-up lag (unsourced): buying a domain, setting up business email and sending tools, building portfolio or demo sites, and vetting each address for CASL all take time before outreach can reach volume, which pushes back the first sale.

Prices for cold-email tools, domains, Google Workspace, hosting, payment-processor fees and business-name registration were not found, so startup costs are unknown beyond the GHL plan prices, which are themselves unverified.

Unsourced but plausible hidden costs: unpaid revision cycles and scope creep on fixed-price builds; ongoing support on AI receptionists or chatbots; clients cancelling monthly retainers; payment delays if deposits are not collected up front; possible liability insurance if an AI tool gives a client's customers wrong information.
HST collection and registration: the threshold was not verified. If the owner registers, prices shown to SMBs need to state whether HST is added (13% in Ontario, rate not verified in this session).
CASL compliance is labour-intensive. Documenting evidence of conspicuous publication for each of ~1,500-3,900 addresses is a large manual workload, and the legal onus is on the owner.
Seasonality (unsourced judgment): starting outreach in October-December overlaps with the holiday rush for restaurants and retail, and some trades slow in winter. No data was found either way.
Regional differences (Montreal): if clients are in Quebec, French-language and Law 25 obligations may apply. Neither was verified in this session.

Currency: US-priced SaaS (GHL and AI receptionists, likely USD) adds foreign-exchange cost and card foreign-transaction fees in CAD terms. Exact impact not calculated, because the currencies are unconfirmed.
verification.verdict: DOWNGRADE, not eliminate. I could not verify any claim: every source domain was egress-blocked and the session search budget was exhausted. The dossier itself rests entirely on search snippets, so the evidence is too weak for a plan the owner's income depends on. The dossier also has a material math error. Its 'about $5.3-5.7k net by day 60' scenario is cumulative two-month revenue, about $3k/month on average, so by its own numbers it misses the $5k/month goal. Its GHL per-client cost derivation is also questionable. Keep it only as a conditional or secondary option: it becomes viable if the owner confirms (a) comfortable business-English or Korean-language selling, (b) existing relationships with local or Korean-owned SMBs who could become first clients, and (c) willingness to do in-person walk-ins. Without those, the chance of averaging CAD $5k/month within 60 days is very low (score 1.5/10). Before relying on it, re-run verification with working web access for these items: the GST/HST threshold, the CASL guide and penalties, the Instantly benchmark, GTA-specific retainer pricing, and GHL plan terms.
